name: Huntington Ingalls Industries
description: Huntington Ingalls is the largest US military shipbuilder. Newport News builds and refuels nuclear-powered aircraft carriers and builds nuclear submarines (it is the only company able to build and refuel carriers); Ingalls in Mississippi builds amphibious assault ships, destroyers and Coast Guard cutters; Mission Technologies sells defense technology services and unmanned systems. About 81 percent of 2025 revenue came from the US Navy, mostly under cost-type (50 percent) and fixed-price-incentive (46 percent) contracts. Backlog was $53.1 billion at year-end 2025.

businessLines.name: Newport News Shipbuilding

businessLines.description: Design and construction of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers (Ford class) and submarines (Virginia class; modules for Columbia class as subcontractor to Electric Boat), plus carrier refueling and overhaul and inactivation.

revenue.note: FY2024 $5,969M (+9%); FY2023 $6,133M. Segment revenue is before $145M of intersegment eliminations; share is of consolidated $12,484M.

businessLines.name: Ingalls Shipbuilding
businessLines.how: The US Navy and Coast Guard pay on long-term ship construction contracts; recognised over time. It is the sole US builder of amphibious assault ships, which gives visibility but margins depend on cost control (about 7.6 percent in 2025).
businessLines.description: Non-nuclear ships for the US Navy and Coast Guard: LHA and LPD amphibious assault ships (sole builder), Arleigh Burke destroyers (one of two builders), national security cutters.

businessLines.name: Mission Technologies
businessLines.how: Government customers pay for engineering and technical services on cost-type and time-and-materials contracts and for delivered unmanned systems; labor-heavy with thin margins (about 5 percent). Includes $132M of work sold to HII shipyards.
businessLines.description: All-Domain Operations, Warfare Systems, Global Security and Unmanned Systems groups: technical services, C5ISR, cyber, nuclear and environmental services, unmanned underwater and surface vehicles.
